clinician.trajectory_summary: A 58-year-old patient presented with a 3-month history of exponential growth (specifically 40 days documented) of a round, hard, non-mobile mass in the posterior femoral region, causing discomfort and embarrassment but no pain at initial presentation. The patient was referred to the radiology department for diagnostic evaluation. Imaging workup sequence: (1) Ultrasound revealed an extremely inhomogeneous lesion with disorganized hypo-anechogenic areas with high water content; (2) CT performed next showed a round, smooth lesion with a tiny capsule located in the context of the semitendinosus muscle, causing mass effect and compression, with inhomogeneous density that raised suspicion for malignancy; (3) MRI performed the following day (without contrast due to elevated creatinine) demonstrated a lobulated, inhomogeneous lesion with isointense T1 and hyperintense T2/STIR/PD signal, focal central necrotic/cystic areas, and absence of the fascia tail sign; DWI/ADC imaging confirmed areas of high cellularity with restricted diffusion, further supporting malignancy suspicion. Based on imaging findings concerning for malignancy, an excisional biopsy was performed, which confirmed the diagnosis of myxofibrosarcoma Grade 3 FNCLCC. Following biopsy confirmation, the patient underwent neoadjuvant treatment with radiotherapy followed by chemotherapy to shrink the mass before planned definitive excisional surgery.
